chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from one of the two (peace be upon them both), who said:
Indeed God will not leave the earth without a knowledgeable one, and were it not for that, Truth would not be distinguished from falsehood.

key_terms.الْبَاطِلِ: falsehood — error, deviation, and corrupt teachings
key_terms.الْحَقُّ: the Truth — divine guidance, correct doctrine, and the righteous path
key_terms.عَالِمٍ: knowledgeable one — in Shia theology, refers specifically to the divinely guided Imam who possesses inherited prophetic knowledge

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Kafi teach about why God always maintains a knowledgeable authority on earth?
ai.summary: This hadith from either Imam al-Baqir (AS) or Imam al-Sadiq (AS) asserts the theological principle that God never leaves the earth devoid of a divinely guided, knowledgeable authority. The teaching grounds the doctrine of the Imamate in divine wisdom: without such a presence, humanity would lose the means to distinguish truth from falsehood. This was especially significant for the Shia community, who saw this divine guarantee as proof of the necessity of the Imam as the living guide in every age.
word_analysis: one of the two of them

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th </sup>Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will not Leave the earth without a knowledgeable one<sup>asws</sup>, and had it not been for that, the Truth would not be recognised from the falsehood’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus ibn Muskan from abu Basir from one of them (Imams (a.s.), who has said the following “
Allah does not leave the earth without a ‘Alim (scholar). Without this the truth would not be distinguished from falsehood.”
